record.original_question: Let pi(x) be the number of primes not exceeding x, and let Li(x) be the logarithmic integral used in the prime number theorem approximation pi(x) is approximately Li(x). What is the exact order of the error term pi(x)-Li(x) in the prime number theorem? In particular, what is the optimal asymptotic size of that error term, beyond the conditional bound pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt(x) ln x) that follows if the Riemann hypothesis is true?

evidence.quote: π(x) is the number of primes up to x. Gauss refined his estimate to π(x)≈Li(x), where Li(x) is the logarithmic integral.

Finding the exact order of the error term in the prime number theorem is one of the most famous and important problems in number theory. If Riemann hypothesis is true, then π(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt(x) ln x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x \geq 2$, let $\pi(x)$ denote the number of prime numbers not exceeding $x$, and let
$$\mathrm{Li}(x) = \int_2^x \frac{dt}{\ln t}$$
denote the (offset) logarithmic integral. The prime number theorem asserts that $\pi(x) \sim \mathrm{Li}(x)$ as $x \to \infty$. It is known unconditionally that
$$\pi(x) = \mathrm{Li}(x) + O\!\left(x \exp(-c \sqrt{\ln x})\right)$$
for some absolute constant $c > 0$, and the Riemann Hypothesis (the statement that every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$ has real part $1/2$) is equivalent to the stronger bound
$$\pi(x) = \mathrm{Li}(x) + O\!\left(\sqrt{x}\,\ln x\right).$$
Determine the exact asymptotic order of the error term $\pi(x) - \mathrm{Li}(x)$. More precisely, find the optimal function $E(x)$ such that $\pi(x) - \mathrm{Li}(x) = O(E(x))$ holds and such that $\pi(x) - \mathrm{Li}(x) = \Omega(E(x))$ in the sense that the bound cannot be improved, going beyond the conditional bound $O(\sqrt{x}\,\ln x)$ implied by the Riemann Hypothesis.
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the exact order of the error term in the prime number theorem is a classical open problem, intimately tied to the Riemann Hypothesis (still unproven) and to known oscillation results of Littlewood showing $\pi(x) - \mathrm{Li}(x) = \Omega_\pm(\sqrt{x}\,\ln\ln\ln x / \ln x)$. No sharp asymptotic order is known.

status_evidence.title: Prime-counting function (Wikipedia)
status_evidence.snippet: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the much tighter bound on the error in the estimate for π(x), and hence to a more regular distribution of prime numbers.
status_evidence.claim: The exact order of the PNT error term is unresolved and equivalent to RH for the bound O(sqrt(x) log x).

status_evidence.title: Riemann Hypothesis - Clay Mathematics Institute
status_evidence.snippet: The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems and remains unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: RH is unresolved, hence the conditional sharp bound on pi(x)-Li(x) is not established.
